title: Crash-safe Print Queue mixed-batch recovery and provider outcome fencing

acceptanceCriteria.description: Recovery uses durable per-order state, continues independently safe work after mixed-batch interruption, and never resends provider-pending orders from a stale parent snapshot.
Ambiguous provider operations reconcile through exact receipt identity and durable one-effect fencing; offline failure injection proves no provider redispatch after an unknown outcome.

Active purchase locks, held provider operations, missing post-purchase artifacts, and receipt-resume states are non-retryable or bounded local-tail states and cannot become an automatic fresh purchase.
Selected-rate proof fails closed on unavailable authority and rejects cross-order, cross-account, and shipment-fact mismatch before any provider effect.
Orders renders backend-owned per-order outcomes, retains interrupted jobs, and resumes by opaque job id without minting retry or provider truth in the frontend.
Rate-authority failure, stale proof, provider ambiguity, and existing-label recovery produce distinct backend outcomes; provider ambiguity is never retry-eligible.
PS-444, PS-452, provider-ledger, rate-authority, label recovery, strict TypeScript, production frontend build, browser E2E, and all 57 mandatory source-of-truth gates pass at the reviewed SHA.

DJ supplied the exact required `unlock shipped data` authorization in the active execution conversation; the historical locked-file scope is bounded, backend edit locks, schemas, and the inventory kill switch were not weakened by PS-444, the pre-existing operator-authorized frontend selection unlock remains unchanged, and verification performed no live provider or production data mutation.

sotBypass.details: Durable backend sidecars, purchase locks, rate authorization, and the provider-operation ledger remain authoritative. Routes and UI transport or render those facts.

evidence.proves: The mixed-order fixture resumes independently safe items while fencing ambiguous provider outcomes and keeping them non-retryable.
The Orders UI renders backend outcomes, resumes by job id with an empty body, and never starts a label or print side effect in the mocked browser scenario.
A fake-provider migrated-database integration turns an ambiguous post-dispatch failure into a durable hold and consumes an exact local receipt once.
The migrated worker fixture admits only the current recovery generation, rejects stale claims, and distinguishes infrastructure recovery from provider reconciliation.

migrations.rollbackPlan: PS-444 and the governance closeout add no schema change. The branch's later additive 0073 Print Queue execution-fence and 0074 billing-adjustment migrations are independently owned and must not be removed or downgraded when rolling back PS-444.

rollback.strategy: Forward-revert only the PS-444 implementation and packet while preserving current additive migrations and all durable queue, provider receipt, shipment, and order history. Never delete receipts, replay provider-pending work, or rewrite shipped/cancelled history during rollback.

liveVerification.reason: Behavioral closure is intentionally offline because a live queue or label mutation could buy postage or alter production order and shipment state. Verification used inert environment values, fake providers, migrated local fixtures, and mocked browser requests only.
